compiled_state.description:
## Problem
`aggregate.py`'s `_severity_rank`/`_SEVERITY_RANK` (an ordinal string->int map over the
5-level severity vocabulary) picks the representative finding in a duplicate cluster and
sorts the final merged list, but the numeric `priority` (`validity x impact`) computed by
`pass3_decide` is dropped before findings reach `aggregate.py`: `shim.py`'s
`_to_common_finding` only carries `severity` forward, not `priority`. This is the exact bug
motivating the epic: a high-impact/low-validity finding can rank above a genuinely
high-priority one because ranking is impact-only.

## Approach
1. Thread `priority` (and `decision`) through `code_review/shim.py`'s `_to_common_finding` so
   the common-finding shape `aggregate.py` consumes carries the numeric value already computed
   by `pass3_decide` (or set on DET-tier findings by the sibling priority-backfill ticket).
2. Replace `aggregate.py`'s `_severity_rank`/`_SEVERITY_RANK` with a direct read of
   `finding["priority"]` at both call sites: representative selection (`aggregate_findings`)
   and the final sort. Delete `_severity_rank`/`_SEVERITY_RANK`.
3. Update `spec_scan.py`'s import/use of `_severity_rank` to sort by `priority` directly.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `shim.py::_to_common_finding` includes `priority` in its output dict for every finding.
- [ ] `aggregate.py::aggregate_findings` selects the cluster representative by
  `finding["priority"]` (ties broken as today by detail length); `_severity_rank` and
  `_SEVERITY_RANK` are deleted.
- [ ] `spec_scan.py` sorts by `priority` instead of the deleted `_severity_rank` import.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_aggregate.py` (locate via
  `pytest --collect-only -q -k aggregate`) passes, with a strengthened test asserting a
  higher-impact/lower-validity finding no longer wins representative selection over a
  lower-impact/higher-validity one with higher priority.
- [ ] `grep -rn "_severity_rank\|_SEVERITY_RANK" src/rebar/llm/` returns no matches.

## Testing
Tier: in-process unit test against the real `aggregate_findings`/representative-selection
function, fed production-shaped finding dicts (contract test: real producer shape -> real
consumer). Oracle: which finding is selected as representative and the sort order of the
merged list, asserted by finding identity. Contrast case: a high-impact/low-validity finding
(low priority) paired with a moderate-impact/high-validity one (higher priority) -- assert
the second wins.
compiled_state.title: Rank aggregation by priority instead of severity
